Source: http://www.vancouverprovince.com/

Posted October 4, 2000
(MarijuanaNews note: Canada is in the midst of a great national debate about the " drug war " in general and marijuana prohibition in particular.
See
Canadian Health Minister Supports " Decriminalization " and Medical Marijuana. Apparently…

The people -- and even the politicians -- seem to be earnestly struggling with the issues. In this context, it is all the more important that the media play a constructive role. This is an obligation that The Vancouver Province is failing badly.

The Province is a tabloid owned by Southam [which is owned by Hollinger, which was just acquired by another Canadian media company…] the same company that owns the Vancouver Sun, a quality broadsheet, and many other papers, including the Ottawa Citizen. Its sister paper, the Sun, serialized the great Ottawa Citizen series by Dan Gardner attacking the drug war, but the editors of the Province seem to have missed it.

Certainly, they must have missed a column that Gardner wrote as a closing comment on the subject.


See
Author of Ottawa Citizen Series on Prohibition Blames The Media for the Drug War. Great Journalism Is The Antidote.

It is natural for tabloids to be more " sensationalistic " in their style and choice of stories, but that does not excuse bad journalism. The problem with these stories is that, except for quoting a brief comment by a B. C. judge, they never question anything that the police say,

In fact, the Province seems intent on proving Gardner’s point: " The media are painfully credulous in dealing with the police, far more so than with any other institution. "

Consequently, the following articles are nothing more than an exercise in prohibitionist propaganda.

However, it gets worse.

As a " public service, " The Province’s web site offers " special reports " on a variety of services. The link to " Teens and Drugs " has a section on marijuana that is low grade reefer madness. [See below]

Newspapers are supposed to care about their credibility. The Province, by pushing prohibitionist propaganda as news and reefer madness as drug education, is undermining its credibility with Canadians who are increasingly fed up with the drug war in general and marijuana prohibition particular.

Perhaps even worse, they are undermining the credibility of all " drug education " and all societal institutions by lying to kids about marijuana. They will grow up distrusting The Province, which is bad for the paper, but also distrusting everyone, which undermines civil society.)
See
The Theory and Practice of Chaos – Analysis By Richard Cowan

October 1, 2000
From The Vancouver Province
provedpg@pacpress.southam.ca
http://www.vancouverprovince.com/
By Salim Jiwa

$3.3 Billion Going Up In Smoke

Marijuana has become a cash crop worth a whopping $3.3 billion in B.C., thanks to a history of low sentences for growers, police say.
(MarijuanaNews note: " Thanks to " = cause and effect? Would there be significantly less marijuana grown here if the sentences were higher. This is a recurring theme of many such stories.
See
From Vancouver To Miami Indoor Marijuana Cultivation Produces Prohibitionist Propaganda, But A Clear Sense That Marijuana Prohibition Is A Disaster. 2 Articles
and
Time Magazine Is Improving On The Party Line On " B. C. Bud. " Now it averages 30% THC! That is really B. S. Bud!
and
How The New York Times Misleads Americans About the Canadian Marijuana Situation.

However, this overlooks the fact that DEAland, which has Draconian sentences for growing, produces half of all the marijuana it consumes, vastly more than Canada produces.

In any case, no one really knows how much marijuana is produced in B. C. But if we take these numbers at face value, does it really make sense for the province to shut down such a huge money maker, especially at a time when its economy is relatively weak?)



The Organized Crime Agency of B.C. estimates organized crime controls almost 75 per cent of the lucrative grow operations, with the Hells Angels holding a 60 per cent stake. Approximately 15 per cent is in the hands of smaller cartels like Vietnamese gangs.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is absolutely no basis in fact for these estimates. There have been very few arrests of bikers in conjunction with grow ops. This year most of the arrests have been of Vietnamese growers, but they are easier to bust than middles class whites.

According to an excellent article by journalist Ken MacQueen in the May 12th Vancouver Sun, the Criminal Intelligence Service Canada report for 1999 says that " Vietnamese criminals in Vancouver now are responsible for approximately 80 per cent of the hydroponic marijuana grow operations that are investigated by the police. "

Now which is it? 15% or 80%?

Or neither? After all, there is a long history of racism in Canadian marijuana prohibition, just as in DEAland.)
See
The Racist Origins Of Canada’s Marijuana Prohibition Reported In the National Post.

There are an estimated 10,000 marijuana farms in B.C., of which 8,000 are in the Lower Mainland.

Alex Tyakoff, a tactical analyst for the crime agency, said a police blitz in April shut down 80 grow ops across B.C. and resulted in the arrest of 96 men and women aged 17 to 45.
(MarijuanaNews note: At that rate they would take out around 10% of their estimated 10,000 grow ops annually, which at least fits the standard estimates by law enforcement that they get 10% of any contraband, but it is still just a guess... and pointless.)

Some 14,258 marijuana plants with a value of $8.2 million were seized, he said.

A month earlier, 90 cops executed 24 search warrants in Burnaby, Vancouver and Surrey. They charged 31 people and took nine children into the care of the Children's Ministry.
(MarijuanaNews note: These tend to be the children of Vietnamese immigrants who don’t know how to defend their rights in Canada. The children were not in any danger, and are invariably reported to be well-fed and well-cared for, but they are still seized -- for their own good, of course!)

Tyakoff said a new police data-base has been developed to target grow ops.

Currently 30 police agencies are contributing data, including U.S. bodies such as the Drug Enforcement Agency, the Border Patrol and Customs Service.
(MarijuanaNews note: Think about that. 30 police agencies, plus the DEA, the Border Patrol and Customs Service! There is an enormous vested interest in marijuana prohibition.)
See
Canadian Police Lie to The Canadian Media Who Lie To Their Readers
To Justify More Power Over the Canadian People To Please DEAland Narks
An Utterly Wretched Piece Of Pseudo-journalism

Massive volumes of B.C. bud are smuggled into the U.S., where authorities have all but declared B.C. a source province for marijuana. Such a declaration would result in the imposition of trade and other sanctions by the U.S.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is truly nonsense. All this reporter has done is to parrot what some nark has told him. First, B. C. is not a major source of DEAland marijuana.
See
INS Report On Canadian Border Uses Numbers to Deceive, But Ends by Contradicting Party Line.
and
RCMP Report On Marijuana Trafficking Contradicts The Party Line
About Marijuana Smuggling From Canada To DEAland. Far More Goes North Than South

Second, if DEAland has not imposed " trade and other sanctions " against Mexico, which supplies perhaps 100 times as much marijuana as B. C. , then why – and how – would it impose such sanctions against Canada?)

See
Someone Floats A Rumor That DEAland Wants To Blacklist Canada;
Washington Denies Everything, But Canadian Prohibitionists Seem To Cheer,
Sort Of… 3 Articles

The U.S. recently declared the I-5 corridor from B.C. to California a high-density trafficking area, which U.S. authorities say is a " dubious " distinction recognizing B.C. as a major source of the drug.

(MarijuanaNews note: Yes, it is " dubious. " First, this is a political pork barrel for the narks.

Second, other high-density drug trafficking areas include the South Florida and New York on the East Coast of DEAland, the Southwestern border, Houston Texas, and now even Appalachia, because of marijuana cultivation. Recently, one of Montana's Senators introduced a bill to get his whole state declared a HDDTA, blaming meth labs! )

A recent U.S. anti-drug project, dubbed Project 49 identified more than 450 B.C. gang members suspected of taking drugs across the border.


Cpl. John Furac, who was in charge of Surrey RCMP's Green team from 1995 to 1998, has helped bust hundreds of grow ops. He said police action does not mean much without harsher sentences by B.C. judges.

" All we need is one judge who makes a bad decision and the rest of them follow saying this is a precedent, " he said. " It is very frustrating. We grab this guy one day and he is out the next day or next hour. And the community is suffering the impact, from home invasions on the serious side to attracting undesirables into an area. " (MarijuanaNews note: All we need is one judge who does not listen to lying narks. Fortunately, B. C. has several such judges. See the next articles below.)

From The Vancouver Province
provedpg@pacpress.southam.ca
http://www.vancouverprovince.com/
By Salim Jiwa

HOW MANY DO THE COPS CATCH?

B.C. judges may have to deal with the disparity in sentencing of marijuana growers in B.C. and Alberta says B.C. Supreme Court Justice Wally Oppal.

But Oppal says there is no evidence higher sentences will work.

" I agree with you that there shouldn't be an inordinate disparity, " he said. " We are going to have to get more consistent. Either Alberta is too high or we are too low.

" But I have to ask: Is Alberta better off than we are?

" There is nothing to indicate that they are better off, other than the fact that the police probably feel better because they are getting higher sentences.
See
Poll Shows B.C. Residents Reject DEAland Pressure To Increase Penalties on Marijuana Growing.

" The police always have to remember that we have to take a balanced look at it. It is perfectly logical for the police to be unhappy about sentences because they do all the investigating but it's also logical to remember that we have more than just crime to think about - we have to think about the background of the offender or whether he has a previous record.

" Put this down: If the police want to blame the courts, I put it to the police, how many people are they catching? "

October 1, 2000
From The Vancouver Province
provedpg@pacpress.southam.ca
http://www.vancouverprovince.com/
By Salim Jiwa

JUDGES SHOW A SOFT SPOT FOR MARIJUANA GROWERS

Judges in B.C. are far softer on marijuana growers than their Alberta counterparts, a Province probe shows.

In B.C., people convicted of running major marijuana grow operations routinely are sentenced to three to six months, and rarely more than a year.

In Alberta they draw terms of up to four years.

The maximum sentence is seven years.

" I think statistically that is right, " said former B.C. Supreme Court Justice Lloyd McKenzie, who represents judges of the B.C. Supreme Court and the B.C. Court of Appeal.

" There is a variance of philosophy of sentencing in Alberta and British Columbia. I know that the fact is that they are inclined to impose heavier sentences. "

McKenzie questioned whether harsher sentences would have any impact on pot-growing.

And B.C. Supreme Court Justice Wally Oppal asked: " Is Alberta better off than we are? There's nothing to indicate they are. "

B.C. police say the disparity in sentencing has turned B.C. into a mecca for pot farmers.

" We would like to see higher sentences, " said Staff-Sgt. Chuck Doucette of the RCMP's drug awareness program.
(MarijuanaNews note: Doucette is quoted in a 1998 Province article as saying, " The new marijuana is highly addictive. The experts are seeing a rapid increase in behavioral problems among users. There are acts of aggression, leading to assaults and even murders. " )
See
Marijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety --
" Is Marijuana Stronger Than It Was Back In the '60s, When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless? "
Analysis By Richard Cowan

" We are saying the drug growers are not being discouraged. They are coming from other provinces here, organized criminals are getting involved in marijuana growing because there aren't any deterrents. "

Doucette claimed court sentences in B.C. are so lenient that crooks who used to distribute hard drugs are now moving here to grow marijuana because it's a " low-risk, high-profit " venture.
(MarijuanaNews note: That’s right. A nark is complaining that " crooks " are getting out of hard drug trafficking and into marijuana growing. We couldn’t make this up!)
See
Prohibitionists Recognize That Having Lower Penalties For Marijuana Discourages Hard Drug Trafficking, But Still Don’t Understand What They Are Saying.
and
HOW THE NARCS CREATED CRACK

The Province investigation found that B.C. judges are more likely than Alberta judges to take mitigating factors into account in sentencing, such as the accused's chances of turning his life around or the need to care for family members.
(MarijuanaNews note: Oh, the horror! Taking " into account in sentencing, such as the accused's chances of turning his life around or the need to care for family members. " )

Ronald Reimer, head of federal prosecutions for Alberta, said it is not uncommon for Alberta judges to hand out sentences of three to four years for large grow operations. Smaller operations draw sentences of up to 18 months.

Federal Justice department files for the last seven years show one B.C. judge handed down a three-month sentence to a man growing 1,188 plants. An Alberta judge gave a man with 604 plants three and a half years.

Earlier this year, B.C. Supreme Court Justice Allan Stewart was cheered by cops for sentencing a first-time offender to two years less a day. He said it was time to up the ante for growers, saying they were putting innocent people at risk.

The B.C.Court of Appeal cut the sentence in half....
